settings.name_in_paper: Linear contextual bandit with endogenous covariates and instrumental variables
unmapped: Covariates are endogenous: noise may be correlated with the context (E[eps_t|v_t] != 0)
Learner observes instrumental variables z_t in R^q (q >= Kp) with E[z_t eps_t]=0
Per-arm linear reward mu_i(v)=v^T alpha_i with arm-specific parameter (d = p per arm)
settings.definition_quote: At each time $t=1,\ldots,T$, the agent observes a vector of covariates $\BFv_t\in\Real^p$, takes an action (i.e., pulls an arm) $a_t\in \{1,\ldots,K\}$ with $K\geq 2$, and receives a random reward $R_t = \sum_{i=1}^K \ind(a_t=i) \mu_i(\BFv_t) +\varepsilon_t$ ... $\mu_i(\BFv) = \BFv^\intercal \BFalpha_i$ ... the covariates are endogenous---that is, $\mathbb{E}[\varepsilon_t|\BFv_t]\neq 0$.

settings.name_in_paper: Two-armed linear contextual bandit with endogenous covariates (IV-Greedy without Phase 2)
unmapped: Covariates are endogenous: noise may be correlated with the context
settings.definition_quote: Suppose there are $K=2$ arms. If the Covariance Stabilization Phase takes $t=T_1+1,...,T_2$ with $T_2-T_1 = C>0$ being an absolute constant...

conditions: eps_t sub-Gaussian with variance proxy varsigma^2
valid instruments E[z_t eps_t]=0, q >= Kp
bounded covariates and instruments ||v_t||_inf <= v_bar, ||z_t||_inf <= z_bar
Sigma*_vz full rank and Sigma_zz positive definite
margin condition: P(|v_t^T delta_ij| <= c) <= L c for all c>0
tuning: T_1 = C_T1 log(T), T_2 = (C_T1 + C_T2) log(T) with sufficiently large constants C_T1, C_T2 (Assumption 2)

source.label: theo:IV-Greedy-regret
source.quote: Let $\ttR = C_{\ttR} \log(T)$ and $\ttU = (C_{\ttR} + C_{\ttU}) \log(T)$ for some sufficiently large constants $ C_{\ttR}$ and $C_{\ttU}$.  Then, under Assumption~\ref{assump:IV}, the regret of the IV-Greedy algorithm is $\mathcal{O}(\log(T))$.

results.notes: Regret is defined through means mu_i(v_t) against the oracle per-context arm, so pseudo-regret vs best action per round. Proof gives explicit bound [sqrt(p) v_bar delta_bar (C_T1+C_T2) + 16(K-1) L p q^3 v_bar^2 z_bar^2 varsigma^2 kappa_bar^2] log T + const. Remark 2 says a doubling trick removes knowledge of T.

bound.regime: T large enough; with probability at least p_lower > 0

symbols.p_lower: positive probability with which non-convergence occurs

conditions: applies to the IV-Greedy algorithm whose Covariance Stabilization Phase has constant length T_2 - T_1 = C independent of T

source.label: prop:Non-Convergence
source.quote: Suppose there are $K=2$ arms. If the Covariance Stabilization Phase takes $t=T_1+1,...,T_2$ with $T_2-T_1 = C>0$ being an absolute constant that does not depend on $T$, then, for any $T$ large enough, there exists $\underline{p}>0$ such that with probability at least $\underline{p}$, one of the two arms does not converge in the IV-Greedy algorithm, leading to a sub-optimal policy and a linear regret.

results.notes: Negative result for a specific algorithm variant; linear regret holds with a constant positive probability, not w.p. 1-delta. Proof is sketchy.

cited_results.setting_description: Standard (exogenous) linear contextual bandit; lower bound for any algorithm
